content: The primary responsibility for implementing the activities outlined in national rabies elimination plans lies with the respective countries. These national plans should be consulted for specific details regarding responsibilities, targets, and progress indicators. Using the objectives described in the global strategic plan as a foundation, a detailed work plan will be developed to guide implementation. This work plan will include a monitoring framework with clearly defined and aligned milestones to measure progress. The United Against Rabies collaboration will execute activities according to this work plan and evaluate progress against the major objectives outlined in the global strategic plan. Annual reports will be provided, detailing both quantitative and qualitative outputs. Additionally, shared tools, templates, and guidance will be reviewed at regular intervals. At the end of each phase, a summary of lessons learned will be published, and this knowledge will be used to inform and adjust activities and budgets for subsequent phases. Each year, partners in the United Against Rabies collaboration will invite stakeholders from various sectors, including countries, regions, academia, and public and private organizations, to share progress and contribute expertise as efforts advance toward the Zero by 30 goal. The greatest risk identified is a slow start to the initiative. However, the four organizations forming the United Against Rabies collaboration are committed to working together to achieve the Zero by 30 target, regardless of funding challenges. The Zero by 30 initiative provides a mid-term horizon that necessitates immediate action. Recent modeling studies indicate that this goal is achievable if the critical supportive mechanisms are implemented without delay. Rabies has persisted for far too long, and the current global momentum must be harnessed to seize this opportunity to end human rabies deaths. Successful elimination efforts in countries supported during Phase 1 will ensure rapid progress toward the global goal and generate momentum to drive further country engagement. The global strategic plan is a catalytic proposal, and investment in this plan will accelerate the growth, delivery, and impact of activities. Advocacy for investment in rabies elimination is essential to strengthen health systems and save lives. Collaboration with countries is ongoing to develop sustainable resource mobilization strategies for implementing national plans. Strong health systems act as sentinels, as disease outbreaks can divert attention and resources from core prevention programs. A cross-sectoral approach promotes national elimination plans and prioritizes health system strengthening. By building country capacity and integrating rabies control with other health system-strengthening measures, the value of country ownership in disease control will be demonstrated. This approach will encourage countries to invest further in successful disease control programs. Health and surveillance systems capable of detecting and preventing endemic diseases, particularly in underserved rural areas, are critical for identifying and responding to emerging diseases. Robust national rabies control programs can integrate with epidemic response mechanisms to increase access and reach populations at risk. Monitoring progress and managing risks are essential components of the strategy. Achieving Zero by 30 will save the lives of children and protect the livelihoods of adults. Vulnerable rural communities will no longer bear the heavy economic burden imposed by rabies, such as lost income or livestock. Most importantly, no one will suffer or die from this preventable disease. Investing in rabies elimination strengthens health systems, improves equity and access to healthcare, and contributes to sustainable development. Capacity-building efforts required for rabies elimination represent an investment not only in eradicating a fatal but preventable disease but also in enhancing capacity in the world's most neglected regions and improving access to health services within these communities. For the first time in history, there is a united effort to leverage existing knowledge, tools, and technology in innovative ways. Now is the time to act, gather political will, engage and empower stakeholders, and make the societal changes necessary to achieve Zero by 30. The United Against Rabies collaboration is already working with countries to coordinate and catalyze global change. Investing in rabies elimination will accelerate progress as the world strives to make this goal a reality by 2030. Rabies elimination is feasible, and the time to act is now.
